children: was selected as one of 15 companies eligible to compete for work under a U.S. Space Force contract vehicle valued at more than $980 million, expanding the space infrastructure company's opportunity to win national security business.

The multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract was awarded through Space Systems Command for the National Space Test and Training Complex Innovative Technology and Engineering - Space Test and Range program, known as NITE-STAR.

can compete for task orders involving the design, development, integration, testing and sustainment of space-based and ground-based systems. The work is intended to strengthen U.S. national security space testing infrastructure and operational readiness.
For investors, the award adds another potential channel for Redwire

to expand its defense and national security space business as the Pentagon increases investment in space capabilities. However, the headline value requires an important qualification: the more than $980 million represents the ceiling for the overall contract vehicle, not an award to Redwire. As one of 15 selected vendors, Redwire isn't guaranteed any revenue and will have to compete for individual task orders.
said the contract fits its strategy of supplying spacecraft systems, digital engineering technology and infrastructure for U.S. national security customers.

The selection also gives Redwire another opportunity to deepen its relationship with the Space Force. The company has been expanding its national security portfolio alongside its broader space infrastructure business, making future task-order awards under NITE-STAR the key development for investors to watch.

title: Redwire lands spot on $980M Space Force contract vehicle
